newsitem.title: USA: Aquarion seeks rate hike for new water plant.
newsitem.headline: Aquarion seeks rate hike for new water plant.

text.p: Aquarion Co said Friday that its BHC subsidiary has asked the Connecticut Department of Public Utility Control to reopen its 1996 rate case, requesting a $2.5 million or 3.4 percent increase in water service rates.
The company said BHC is seeking the increase to help fund construction and operating costs of its largest federally mandated filtration plant at its Hemlocks Reservoir in Fairfield.

The facility will cost about $47.5 million, said the company, and has a treatment capacity of 50 million gallons of water per day. It is is expected to be completed this summer, and the Aquarion said it anticipates the new rates will become effective in the third quarter of 1997.

Aquarion is engaged primarily in the supply and protection of public water. Its BHC and Sea Cliff Water Company subsidiaries together are, says the company, among the largest investor-owned water utilities in the U.S.
